outcome: at-risk classification based on screening tools
cohort: 509 children screened from informal settlements in Nairobi, Kenya, and a comparative sample from Italy.
finding: 8.6% of the 509 children screened were classified as at-risk for neurodevelopmental disorders, with significant risk factors including history of low birth weight, Apgar score, neurological disorders, malnutrition/rickets, younger age of the child, and older age of the mother.
mod_finding: Caesarean section delivery was identified as a common risk factor for neurodevelopmental disorders among both the Kenyan and Italian samples.
cross-section timing: Early screening for neurodevelopmental disorders, including toddlers (M-CHAT-R), with varying child ages where younger age was a risk factor.
